summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Deleanu studied at Waseda University under Fumimasa Fukui and Takashi Iwata, and earned a PhD at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and Harunaga Isaacson. He held professorships at Kansai Medical University and ICPBS.
Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Naples Federico II from around 2015 to 2018 and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" around 2019.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Sferra studied under Raffaele Torella. He held posts as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (circa 2005) and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010), and served as Direttore at Series Minor.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (1778–1783) and served in the Indian Medical Service from around 1794 to 1815, succeeding Henry Thomas Colebrooke.

Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of the Asiatic Society (1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College from 1801 to 1805.

Francis H. Cook worked in Buddhist and religious studies. After completing doctoral thesis requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he taught at the University of California, Riverside (1970–1989) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

Francis N. J. works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and carried out doctoral studies there under the supervision of M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).
Francis Robinson works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Bexhill College and became a professor at Royal Holloway, University of London, around 1973.

Francis Tiso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his education at Cornell University (1968–1972), Harvard Divinity School (1972–1974), and Columbia University (1980–1989).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Harvard University (1933–1942) and spent his academic career teaching there from 1946 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and Chicago (doctorate, 1984), he was a professor at Boston College, Academic Director at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies, and director at Harvard University.
Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Martin Haug at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1868 to 1871.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, training at the University of Chile and Harvard, and under Chögyam Trungpa and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He held posts at the University of Chile, CNRS, and École Polytechnique, and co-founded Mind & Life Institute.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he held positions at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and the École française d'Extrême-Orient, serving as its director (2004–2014).

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaii under Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya, completing a doctorate under Stewart Sutherland.

Frank Raymond Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of London. He held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Cambridge, and the Ancient India and Iran Trust, and founded the European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art.

Frank-Richard Hamm specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate under Walther Schubring at the University of Hamburg, where he also taught, before serving as Professor für Indologie at the University of Bonn starting in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He taught at Johns Hopkins and the University of Pennsylvania before serving as Salisbury Professor at Yale University from 1926.

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 2002–2006).

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt and completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt. In 1966, he became Professor and seminar director at the University of Hamburg.
